newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mostly weaker on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. treasuries amid some foreign selling linked to the approach of next week's Canadian election, analysts said.

"There was a reasonable amount of long bonds hanging around. I think most of that came from U.S. guys who were playing the Canada-U.S. spread and decided maybe they should take some profits prior to the election," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.19 to C$110.00 to yield 7.148 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond traded unchanged to yield 7.03 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from 11 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
Canadian bonds were also hurt by new supply in the market, analysts said. The Government of Canada this afternoon auctioned C$2.6 billion of 5.5 percent bonds due September 1, 2002.
"(The auction) went okay, but I doubt whether it's fully distributed. There are definitely bonds around," said Altamira's Allan.
The Bank of Canada said its C$2.6 billion auction of 5.5 percent bonds produced an average yield of 6.085 percent, with a low yield of 6.08 percent and high yield of 6.093 percent.
Bids from primary dealers totaled C$5,557.9 million, including C$60.4 million non-competitive tenders at the average yield. The outstanding debt of the issue now totals C$5.3 billion.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.07 to C$102.65 to yield 6.619 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.0 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.13 percent.
